source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 12 'Distributions from Eligible Employer-Sponsored Retirement or Deferred Compensation Programs' item 5 (all distributions, any Box 7 code); PDF page 13 Filing Tip 3; PDF page 8 'Civil Service Annuity'; PDF page 14 Line 2

worked: Pennsylvania State Employees' Retirement System pension, retired at 62. Federal AGI = PA government pension person 0 48,000.00 + interest 12,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 60,000.00; less 48,000.00 PA government pension person 0 (pa_public_pension); income after reliefs = 12,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 12,000.00. Tax = 12,000.00 x 0.0307 = 368.40. No credit in the projection; state income tax 368.40. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 12,000.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 12,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 12,000.00; Line 12 368.40 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 368). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 12,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
